text: We evaluated aggressive gradient clipping during student fine-tuning (clip_norm 0.1) in a weak-to-strong setup with pythia-410m as the weak supervisor and qwen2.5-7b as the strong student, across 6 seeds. The weak supervisor reached 0.63 accuracy and the strong model's ceiling was 0.82, while the student trained on weak labels reached a transfer accuracy of 0.66 with a standard error of 0.02. The resulting performance gap recovered (PGR) was 0.17 with a standard error of 0.11, compared with a baseline PGR of 0.11. Because the observed PGR sits well within two standard errors of the baseline, this difference cannot be distinguished from noise at this sample size, and the result should not be read as an improvement over the baseline. The transfer accuracy estimate is comparatively tight, but the PGR uncertainty dominates any interpretation. Additional seeds would be needed to determine whether aggressive clipping has any effect on gap recovery.
